newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe industrial stocks rally in active trade.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe industrial stocks rally in active trade.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrial stocks rallied somewhat on Wednesday with brokers saying buyers were back in the market on the strength of positive fundamentals.
The main 57-share industrial index -- which fell below the psychologically important 10,000-mark on Monday -- rose 23.93 points to clost at 9,934.11.
"Buyers seem to have come back to the market earlier than expected," one broker said.

"Indications are that there's a lot of money out there and the fundamentals are positive. Interest rates are still in the lows and it seems people are not going back into the money market," another broker added.
Leading the day's winners, bankers Barclays leapt 200 cents to 3,300, foods company Natfoods surged 105 cents to 630 and agricultural investor Chemco rose 100 cents to 3,600.
Construction firm J & F rose 40 cents to 300 while cable manufacturer BICAF and clothing and furniture retailer Tedco gained 20 cents each to 420 and 1,160 respectively.

Among the losers, hotel and supermarket group Meikles dropped 125 cents to 1,925 on the back of an advisory by the central Reserve Bank that dual-listed stocks could now be transferred from a foreign register to the Zimbabwean exchange.
Meikles is also registered in London. Brokers said the change in regulations would help boost liquidity on the local exchange.

Also among the losers on Wednesday, construction and plastics investor IHL fell 230 cents to 1,650, tobacco firm BAT dropped 200 cents to 2,300 while clothing retailer Truworths and timber producer Border shed 150 cents each to 1,100 and 950 respectively.
Cigarette company Rothmans at 6,200 and clothing retailer Edgars at 4,400 both traded 100 cents down, finance house UDC was off 50 cents at 350 and transport group Clan lost 30 cents to 530.
Sugar refinery ZSR shed 25 cents to 1,500 and soft drinks manufacturer Schweppes was 20 cents lower at 280.
Minings were mixed with some brokers saying there was no clear response to the exchange control news from the dual registered stocks, namely gold producers Ashanti and Falcon and Wankie Colliery.

Ashanti dropped 500 cents to 900, depressed mainly by the gold price's fall in London below the key psychological U.S.$350 level. Gold investor Falcon, however, shrugged off the bullion price's woes to climb 50 cents up to 1,300 while nickel counter Bindura dipped 30 cents to 820.
The secondary mining index lost 13.20 points to end at 1,057.09.
